newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds remain steady despite wary market.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds remain steady despite wary market.

text.p: Irish bonds underperformed most European markets on Wednesday, but were broadly unchanged in moderate to brisk trade, dealers said.
"The curve has flattened and we've seen weakness at the short end," one dealer said. "But despite some nervousness out there, players are showing interest in the market."
By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 12 pence at 101.40 to yield 6.11 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was up three pence at 108.58 to yield 6.71 percent.
Yields against German Bunds were broadly unchanged at 169 basis points over in the five-year bond, and 92 over in the 10-year.
Dealers said the Irish market remained wary following fresh turbulence over EMU, and in the wake of a close-run general election at the weekend.

"Not only are people double-guessing over EMU but effectively we're between governments and not absolutely sure what the new administration is going to do. It's also unclear what way the central bank is going to go on the weak Irish pound," said one.

While European markets were driven in early trade by optimism that an accord on the EU budget stability pact could be signed at the Amsterdam summit next week, a German paper later said Bonn was considering a plan to delay the EMU start by a year and shorten the transition phase for the euro's introduction.
Meanwhile, a Reuters poll showed that economists and analysts believe the chance of a timely 1999 EMU start has fallen to 76 percent from 82 percent in May.
The expectations of a broad-based start to EMU were sharply higher.
Irish CPI figures will be an important focus tomorrow, with most traders expecting them to be supportive of the market.
U.S. retail sales figures are also due.
